title: api-config-runtime-arch-scratchpad-jordan
content:
Quick scratchpad for runtime-facing API config shape. Notes to self and bits to share with Maya/Casey before next sync.

Goal: define a compact, extensible config for per-route inference behavior that can live in both Hosted and Dedicated control planes, and be exportable for Private deployments. Keep runtime decision surfaces small and versioned.

High-level requirements (reminder):
- Route-level controls: model, model_variant, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop_sequences, streaming (bool)
- Runtime controls (pluggable): batching policy, prefix caching, kv-cache retention, quantization profile, fallback policy
- Placement/routing: preferred_region, allowed_regions, capacity_tier (hosted|dedicated|private), model_compatibility_hints
- Observability hooks: telemetry_labels, sampling_rate, response_tracing (enabled|disabled)
- Rollouts: canary_percent, rollout_window_minutes, on_failure_behaviour (rollback|auto-fallback)

Config shape (draft YAML-ish):

route: /compose/email-digest
model: redwood/gptx-1
variant: gptx-1-8bit
max_tokens: 800
temperature: 0.2
top_p: 0.9
streaming: true
stop_sequences: ["\n--END--"]

runtime:
  batching:
    mode: adaptive   # fixed | adaptive | disabled
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_latency_ms: 50
    bucket_by: ["sequence_length", "priority"]
  caching:
    prefix_cache:
      enabled: true
      ttl_seconds: 300
      # note: need to decide on eviction semantics (LRU vs policy)
  kv_cache:
    enabled: true
    retention: per-request   # per-request | session | persistent
  quantization_profile: q4_0  # q8_0 | q4_0 | int8-fast
  fallback:
    model_fallback_order: ["redwood/gptx-1-4bit", "redwood/gptx-1-cpu"]
    on_fail: auto-fallback

placement:
  preferred_region: us-west-2
  allowed_regions: [us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1]
  capacity_tier: hosted

rollout:
  canary_percent: 10
  window_minutes: 30
  on_failure: rollback

observability:
  telemetry_labels: {product: inbox, feature: digest}
  sampling_rate: 0.02
  trace_response: true

Notes / open questions:
- \"bucket_by\" semantics: should we expose sequence-length bucketing explicitly or let runtime infer? Exposing allows predictable batching but burdens product config. Maybe expose high-level options: cost_sensitive | latency_sensitive | balanced.
- prefix_cache ttl: 300s default seems ok, but with user sessions we might want session-scoped caches. Need privacy/security check for persistent caches in Private deployments.
- kv_cache retention modes: \"per-request\" is safe but loses reuse. \"session\" requires session IDs + sticky routing. For Dedicated deployments we can recommend session mode.
- quantization_profile: need a mapping table per-model in catalog -> which profiles are supported and perf/cost delta metadata. Should be validated at config ingestion time.
- fallback ordering: how to express cross-tenant policy? e.g., prefer smaller model within same family before switching families. Will need model affinity tags.
- rollout semantics: if canary_percent > 0 and in Dedicated environment, how to implement: weight-based routing vs shadowing then promote? Implementation tradeoffs.

Runtime implementation notes (high-level):
- At config ingestion (control plane): validate model name + variant + quant profile against model catalog. If mismatch, return 422 + helpful message.
- Translate config into runtime ephemeral policy object with version id (route_config:v20241120-01). Policies are small and should be hot-reloadable.
- Routing component should evaluate: capacity_tier -> region constraints -> model_compatibility -> canary weight -> fallback chain. Keep deterministic tie-breakers.
- Batcher should support dynamic grouping keys: (model, variant, quant_profile, bucket_key). Each route can suggest bucket_key strategy but runtime may override for capacity reasons.
- Telemetry labels flow through request context. Ensure we don't log PII in labels.

Diag (ASCII):
Client --> API Gateway (auth, quotas) --> Route Evaluator --> [Policy Store (cache)] --> Router --> ModelPool A/B/C --> Inference Worker --> Response
                 |                                                       ^
                 +--> Telemetry/Tracing (sampling) ------------------------+

To-dos before next sync with Maya: 
- [ ] draft config JSON schema (openapi?) with examples for chat, embeddings, rerank routes
- [ ] add validation rules and error messages for common misconfigs
- [ ] prototype prefix_cache TTL behaviour in local runtime (small PoC)
- [ ] add test plan: unit tests for policy translation + integration tests with batcher simulator

Random thoughts / heuristics:
- Default to safe values: batching=adaptive, max_latency_ms=50, max_batch_size=64. Let advanced teams tune.
- Expose two UX surfaces: simple mode (concise route config) and advanced mode (full runtime tuning). UI can hide advanced by default.
- Keep placement hints optional; if absent, runtime chooses best region based on latency & cost profile for tenant.

Draft error message examples (for control plane rejection):
- 422 Invalid quantization_profile: q8_1 not supported for model redwood/gptx-1. Supported: q8_0, q4_0.
- 422 Incompatible fallback chain: fallback model redwood/gptx-2 not same family as primary. Confirm?

Sharing: will put a short summary into Confluence RT-Config-Design and link to this scratchpad. Also plan to open a GH design PR with schema + validation code.

-- Jordan
summary: Scratchpad for defining route-level runtime config schema: batching, caching, placement, rollouts, observability. Contains draft config shape, open questions, implementation notes, and next steps.
